prompt.adult: Why did a man from Bethlehem in Judah take his wife and two sons to live in the country of Moab?
prompt.child: Elimelech moved his family from Bethlehem to Moab. Why did they leave home?
prompt.teen: What problem in the land led Elimelech's family to move away to Moab?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 1:1, what happened in the land that led the family to go to Moab?

verses.text: Now it came to pass, in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Bethlehem, Judah, went to dwell in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.

explanation.adult: Ruth 1:1 tells what happened in the days when the judges ruled. Read the first sentence.
explanation.child: Read the first sentence of Ruth 1:1.
explanation.teen: Ruth 1:1 gives the problem first and then tells where the family went.
explanation.older: Ruth 1:1 sets the scene with a time, a hardship, and a move; the hardship comes first.

teaching.extended_explanation: The book of Ruth opens with a hardship that sent a family away from Bethlehem. Read the first sentence of Ruth 1:1.
teaching.takeaway: There was a famine in the land, so the family went to Moab.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Naomi urged her two daughters-in-law to go back. Ruth clung to her, but which daughter-in-law kissed her and went back?
prompt.child: Naomi had two daughters-in-law. Ruth stayed with her. Which one kissed Naomi and went back home?
prompt.teen: When Naomi told them to return home, one daughter-in-law kissed her goodbye while Ruth held on. Who kissed her goodbye?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 1:14, who kissed her mother-in-law?

verses.text: Then they lifted up their voices and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.

explanation.adult: Ruth 1:14 names both daughters-in-law. Find the one who kissed Naomi.
explanation.child: Read Ruth 1:14. Look for the name before "kissed her mother-in-law."
explanation.teen: Ruth 1:14 contrasts two choices with the word "but." Read the part before it.
explanation.older: Ruth 1:14 gives both responses side by side; the first name is the one who kissed Naomi and turned back (see 1:15).

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth 1:14 shows two daughters-in-law making different choices. Read the verse again to find the one who kissed Naomi.
teaching.takeaway: Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and went back, but Ruth clung to Naomi.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Ruth told Naomi that Naomi's people would be her people. What else did Ruth say would be hers?
prompt.child: Ruth promised to stay with Naomi. She said Naomi's people would be her people. What else?
prompt.teen: In her famous promise, Ruth said she would take on Naomi's people. What else did she say she would take as her own?
prompt.older: In Ruth 1:16, besides Naomi's people, what did Ruth claim as her own?

verses.text: But Ruth said: “Entreat me not to leave you, Or to turn back from following after you; For wherever you go, I will go; And wherever you lodge, I will lodge; Your people shall be my people, And your God, my God.

explanation.adult: Ruth 1:16 ends with two promises. Read the last line.
explanation.teen: Ruth 1:16 lists where Ruth would go and lodge, then names two things she would make her own.
explanation.older: Ruth 1:16 builds to its final pair; the last clause is Ruth's confession of faith.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth's promise was about more than where she would live. Read the final line of Ruth 1:16.
teaching.takeaway: Ruth said, "Your people shall be my people, and your God, my God."

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: After Naomi and Ruth arrived in Bethlehem, what did Ruth ask Naomi to let her go to the field and do?
prompt.child: Ruth and Naomi needed food in Bethlehem. What did Ruth ask to go do in the field?
prompt.teen: Ruth wanted to provide for Naomi. What did she ask permission to do in the fields?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 2:2, what did Ruth ask Naomi to let her do?

verses.text: So Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go to the field, and glean heads of grain after him in whose sight I may find favor.” And she said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

explanation.adult: Ruth 2:2 records Ruth's request. Read what she asked to do in the field.
explanation.child: Read Ruth 2:2. Ruth tells Naomi what she wants to do.
explanation.teen: In Ruth 2:2, Ruth asks to go to the field. Find what she planned to do there.
explanation.older: Ruth 2:2 shows Ruth's own initiative. Read what she asked Naomi to let her do in the field.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth looked for a way to feed herself and Naomi. Ruth 2:2 tells what she asked to do. Read it again.
teaching.takeaway: Ruth asked to go to the field and glean heads of grain.

prompt.adult: Ruth asked Boaz why he was being kind to her, a foreigner. What had Boaz heard about her?
prompt.child: Boaz was kind to Ruth. He said he had heard about something she did. What was it?
prompt.teen: Why did Boaz take notice of Ruth? What had been fully reported to him?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 2:11, what had been fully reported to Boaz?

choices.text: She was a wealthy woman from Moab
All she had done for Naomi

verses.text: And Boaz answered and said to her, “It has been fully reported to me, all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you have left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and have come to a people whom you did not know before.

explanation.adult: Ruth 2:11 is Boaz's answer to Ruth's question. Read the first part of what he said.
explanation.child: Read Ruth 2:11. Boaz says what people told him.
explanation.teen: Ruth 2:11 tells what Boaz had heard, then lists what Ruth left behind.
explanation.older: Ruth 2:11 explains Boaz's kindness by what was reported about Ruth since her husband's death.

teaching.extended_explanation: Boaz's kindness came after hearing about Ruth's faithfulness. Read the first half of Ruth 2:11.
teaching.takeaway: Boaz had heard all Ruth had done for her mother-in-law Naomi.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: The close relative gave up his right to redeem Naomi's land. To confirm it, what did he take off?
prompt.child: The relative closer than Boaz said Boaz could redeem the land instead. What did he take off to seal the deal?
prompt.teen: To confirm handing over his right of redemption to Boaz, what did the other relative remove?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 4:7-8, what did the close relative take off to confirm the exchange?

verses.text: Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning redeeming and exchanging, to confirm anything: one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other, and this was a confirmation in Israel.
Therefore the close relative said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.” So he took off his sandal.

explanation.adult: Ruth 4:7 explains the custom, and Ruth 4:8 shows the close relative following it.
explanation.teen: Ruth 4:7 describes how people confirmed a deal in Israel. Find what one man gave the other.
explanation.older: Ruth 4:7 explains an old custom of confirmation, and 4:8 records it being done.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth 4:7 explains an old custom for confirming a redemption. Read Ruth 4:7-8 again to see what the man took off.
teaching.takeaway: The close relative took off his sandal to confirm that Boaz could redeem.

prompt.adult: Boaz married Ruth, and she bore a son. What name did the neighbor women give him?
prompt.child: Ruth and Boaz had a baby boy. What was his name?
prompt.teen: After Ruth became Boaz's wife and had a son, what did the neighbor women call him?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 4:17, what was the son of Ruth and Boaz named?

verses.text: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and when he went in to her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son.
Also the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, “There is a son born to Naomi.” And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

explanation.adult: Ruth 4:13 tells of the marriage and the son. Ruth 4:17 gives his name.
explanation.child: Read Ruth 4:17. Look for "they called his name."
explanation.teen: Ruth 4:17 says the neighbor women named the baby. Find the name.
explanation.older: Ruth 4:17 records the naming and then traces the family line forward.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth 4:13 tells of the birth, and Ruth 4:17 tells what the neighbor women named the child. Read it again.
teaching.takeaway: Ruth and Boaz's son was named Obed.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: The son born to Ruth and Boaz became the grandfather of someone famous. Who?
prompt.child: Ruth's baby grew up and had a son, and that son had a famous son. Who was the famous grandson?
prompt.teen: The book of Ruth ends by connecting this family to a well-known person in Israel. Who is it?
prompt.older: According to Ruth 4:17, who was Jesse the father of?

verses.text: Also the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, “There is a son born to Naomi.” And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

explanation.adult: Ruth 4:17 ends by tracing the family two generations ahead. Read the last sentence.
explanation.child: Read the last sentence of Ruth 4:17. Follow the family line.
explanation.teen: Ruth 4:17 names the baby's son and then the baby's grandson. Find the grandson.
explanation.older: Ruth 4:17 (and the genealogy in 4:18-22) ties this family to a later figure in Israel's history; the last name in 4:17 is the answer.

teaching.extended_explanation: Ruth's faithfulness became part of a much bigger story. Read the last sentence of Ruth 4:17 and follow the line to the end.
teaching.takeaway: Ruth's son became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
